the mitochondrial isolate from S. digitata contains succinate dehydro-genase (SDH), succinate--ubiquinol reductase (SQR) and succinate oxidase activities, and that the succinate oxidizing system in the parasite is different from the mammalian counterpart.
succinate oxidation and FR in S. digitatas are catalysed by different enzyme complexes.
the succinate oxidizing system of S. digitata is different from that of mammalian mitochondria and the parasite is capable of generating ATP from succinate oxidation in the absence of fumarate.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the activities of the succinate dehydrogense and fumarate reducing enzymes in the mitochondria of S. digitata and the response of these enzymes against various modulators and inhibitors of electron transport chain.
the identification of the two enzymes, namely, succinate oxidase and FR of S. digitata and the determination of the effect of various modulators and inhibitors against the two enzyme systems.
the identification of succinate oxidizing and reducing systems in the filarial parasite S. digitata and their response against modulators and inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two systems are distinct, but the activities of the enzymes involved are interdependent and the system is regulated by the substrate and the inhibitors.
SDH of S. digitata has the ability to function as FR.
S. digitata possesses a succinate oxidase complex and a fumarate reductorase system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the succinate oxidising system of Setaria has a unique feature of being catalysed by only SDH and a succinate oxidase.
S. digitata has only two activities namely succinate dehydrogenease and succinate--ubiquinone reductase, which constitute the succinate oxidizing system.
the mitochondrial system of S. digitata is capable of expressing two distinct activities namely FR and succinate oxidase and the latter activity is not a true oxidase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
S. digitata, a filarial parasite from a ruminant, has a succinate oxidase complex that differs from that in other organisms.
the two activities are not identical and that succinate oxidase is a unique system of the parasite.
the two activities namely SDHA and FR in Setaria digitata are not identical and they are not regulated in the same way.
